A second severe storm affected the southern and central sections of Motley County during the afternoon of the 1st. The Matador Fire Department reported nickle size hail in the city.
Golfball size hail was reported along Texas Highway 70 north of Matador.

Several storm chasers photographed a well-developed and long-lived landspout tornado between Roaring Springs and Matador. The tornado remained in open fields near Texas Highway 70. Although the tornado persisted for more than fifteen minutes, no damage resulted.
The Motley County Fire Department reported quarter size hail in rural areas of eastern Motely County.

Trained storm spotters reported very large hail in Roaring Springs. No damage was reported.A pair of splitting supercells developed over the Caprock Escapement during the late afternoon of the 9th. These storms produced large hail. No damage was reported.
A motorist reported quarter size hail over Texas Highway 70 northwest of Matador.

A linear complex of thunderstorms exhibited bow-echo radar characteristics as it impacted southern Motley County during the late afternoon hours of the 26th. The public reported that severe thunderstorm winds downed large tree limbs and numerous electrical lines as the storms imp…
The Texas Tech University West Texas Mesonet recorded a thunderstorm wind gust of 59 miles per hour near Roaring Springs. No damage was reported.
A National Weather Service cooperative observer reported nickel size hail in Flomot.
Storm spotters reported that severe thunderstorm winds downed tree limbs in Northfield.
The Matador Fire Department reported hail up to three-quarter inch diameter in Roaring Springs.
The Motley County Fire Department reported large hail ranging in size from dimes to golf balls along Farm to Market Road 684 west of Roaring Springs.
The public reported quarter size hail just east of Flomot at the intersection of Farm to Market Roads 97 and 2009.
A second severe storm impacted the Flomot vicinity, and quarter size hail fell at the intersection of Farm to Market Roads 97 and 2007 twice in a one hour period. No damage was reported.
The Matador Fire Department reported dime to nickel size hail along a swath of U.S. Highway 62/70 southwest of Matador.

Local newspapers reported that utility poles were downed by thunderstorm winds near the Whiteflat community, along Texas Highway 70 north of Matador. Power outages impacted the surrounding area until 03:00 CST on the 17th.
The Matador Fire Department reported that hail up the size of quarters covered the ground in Matador. No damage was reported.
Heavy rainfall was accompanied by a few penny size hail stones east of Flomot at 17:30 CST.
Skywarn storm spotters reported a swath of large hail up to the size of golf balls from seven miles northeast of Matador to Matador. No damage was reported.
Severe thunderstorm winds blew down several utility poles along U.S. Highway 62/70 east of Matador. Power outages resulted with an unknown number of rural customers affected.
The Texas Tech University West Texas Mesonet measured a 61 mph downburst wind gust as an otherwise weak convective shower impacted southern Motley County. No damage was reported.
The Texas Tech University West Texas Mesonet station recorded a severe thunderstorm wind gust of 58 mph just north of Roaring Springs. No damage was reported.
Multiple reports of golfball size hail were received from storm chasers along Texas Highway 70 northwest of Matador shortly after 17:00 CST.
A National Weather Service cooperative observer reported penny size hail northwest of Matador.
The public reported penny size hail along Farm to Market Road 94 just south-southwest of Northfield.
The Matador Fire Department reported golfball size hail in Roaring Springs. No damage was reported.
Local fire department officials reported two inch diameter hail in Matador at 16:35 CST. Minor damages to vehicles and roofs occurred.
An off-duty National Weather Service employee reported giant two and a half inch diameter hail in Matador. Minor damages to vehicles and roofs occurred.
A National Weather Service cooperative observer reported quarter size hail near Northfield.

Multiple storm chasers observed a large and rain-wrapped tornado that moved east-northeastward across the Motley and Cottle County line south-southeast of Northfield and southwest of Cee Vee during the 18:00 CST hour on the 22nd. ||Doppler radar, along with post-storm ground and …
A National Weather Service cooperative observer reported golfball size hail that intermittently mixed with larger two inch-diameter hailstones at Northfield. No damages were reported.
A National Weather Service cooperative observer reported that very large tennis ball hailstones intermittently mixed with more numerous golfball size hail at Northfield. No damages were reported.
The public reported penny size hail in Matador.
The Matador Fire Department reported quarter size hail along U.S. Highway 62/70 in eastern Motley County. Rotation was additionally visible at the cloud's base.
Law enforcement officials estimated thunderstorm wind gusts to be in excess of 60 mph. No damage was reported.
The Matador Fire Department reported that thunderstorm winds downed several utility lines along Texas Highway 70 north of Matador.
The Texas Tech University West Texas Mesonet site near Northfield recorded a peak thunderstorm wind gust of 61 mph at 20:00 CST. No damage was reported.
The public reported that quarter size hail briefly accompanied a thunderstorm at Northfield shortly after 14:00 CST.
Broadcast media relayed a public report of golf ball sized hail in Matador. No damage was reported.
The public reported golf ball size hail north of Matador. No damage was reported.
Fire department personnel estimated quarter size hail 6W Matador. No damage was reported.

The public reported dime size hail with a few quarter-size hailstones in Northfield. No damage was reported.
Measured by a Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet.
Measured by a Texas Tech University West Texas Mesonet station.
Hail up to 1.25 inches was observed 12S Northfield. No damage was reported.
Wind-driven hail damaged crops four miles northeast of Flomot. An unknown amount of damage to the crops occurred.
Measured by a Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet site.
A Texas Tech University West Texas Mesonet station about one mile south of Northfield observed a 67 mph severe thunderstorm wind gust.
A Texas Tech University West Texas Mesonet station north of Roaring Springs observed a 58 mph severe thunderstorm wind gust.
A cooperative observer in Northfield reported hail as large as walnuts along with high winds of unknown intensity for about 3 minutes. No damage was reported.
Fire department personnel from Roaring Springs estimated mostly quarter size hail with some golf ball size hailstones in the city. Damage, if any, was unknown.
A local fire department official observed quarter size hail north of Matador. Additionally, damage to trees and roofs were reported on the north side of Matador.
The Texas Tech University West Texas Mesonet site in Roaring Springs measured a 60 mph wind gust.
Law enforcement reported numerous trees and one power line down in the Flomot area. Also, an estimated 25 center pivot irrigation systems were overturned and damaged nearby.

A NWS Cooperative Observer reported tree limbs broken, shingles blown off a roof and a stock trailer blown 200 feet by severe winds. Although a Texas Tech University West Texas Mesonet station located one mile south of Northfield only measured a peak gust of 57 mph at 4:05 pm CST…
A SKYWARN Spotter observed quarter size hail east southeast of Flomot.

The COOP observer in Matador reported a damaged Fischer Porter precipitation gauge. The damage was caused from a blow by a pig shelter that became airborne in severe winds.
Measured by a Texas Tech University West Texas Mesonet station near Northfield. A gust to 58 mph occurred at 1550 CST.
Law enforcement personnel reported multiple trees were downed in Matador.
A citizen in Matador forwarded a photo to the NWS Lubbock staff of large hail up to 1.25 inches in diameter. Damage information was not available.
Both the emergency manager for Motley County and Matador fire department reported hail to the size of golf balls in the city of Matador.

Storm spotters and fire department officials from Matador reported a swath of large hail up to golf ball size accompanied by destructive downburst winds. The wind-driven hail damaged dozens of vehicles, broke some north-facing windows to homes and businesses in and near Matador, …

Downburst winds in the rear flank downdraft of a supercell caused scattered wind damage in Matador and also overturned a semi-truck on US Highway 62 east of Matador. The driver was not injured. Wind damage in and around Matador consisted of a portion of a roof removed from a hous…
Measured by a Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet near Northfield.
Severe hail from quarter to 1.5 inches in diameter was reported from Matador to Northfield. Damage was unknown.
The emergency manager in Motley County reported two inch size hail east of Matador. No damage was reported.

A storm chaser observed wind-driven hail as large as tennis balls. The hail fell immediately west of what would become a significant tornado just a few minutes later. Minor hail damage occurred to the storm chaser's vehicle.

An NWS cooperative weather observer reported wind damage to his cotton crop.

An NWS cooperative weather observer near Matador reported baseball ball size hail. There was an unknown amount of damage to vehicles in the area.

The first of several tornadoes developed approximately seven miles north of Matador. Storm chasers stated that there was a brief tornado touchdown over open ranch land. No known damage occurred.

An emergency management official and NWS cooperative weather observer reported hail ranging in size from baseballs to 4.50 inches in diameter.
A Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet site near Roaring Springs measured severe wind gusts from 1922 CST through 1928 CST. A peak wind gust of 75 mph was measured at 1922 CST.
The fourth of several tornadoes occurred approximately four miles west of Matador. Local broadcast media live streamed a tornado that crossed US Highway 62. No known damage occurred.

A Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet site near Roaring Springs measured severe wind gusts from 1951 CST through 1958 CST. A peak wind gust of 80 mph was measured at 1953 CST. There was minor damage to the mesonet site.
A Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet site near Roaring Springs measured a wind gust to 59 mph.

An NWS cooperative weather observer estimated wind gusts of 80 mph lasting for approximately 20 minutes. No damage was reported.

A Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet site near Flomot measured severe wind gusts from 1743 CST through 1750 CST. A peak wind gust of 90 mph was measured at 1744 CST.

Multiple storm chasers published photograph and video evidence of a large tornado that crossed over open ranch land from Floyd County into Motley County. No damage was reported or found with this tornado. However, trees and shrubs were lofted and power flashes observed on chaser …

A report from the public was received of hail measuring five inches in diameter. This hail was from the same swath in Floyd County which produced hail up to 5.20 inches in diameter. No damage was reported.
Law enforcement in Motley County observed a brief tornado over open fields west of Roaring Springs. No damage was reported.
A Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet site near Roaring Springs measured severe wind gusts from 1633 CST through 1635 CST. A peak wind gust of 64 mph was measured between 1633 and 1634 CST.
A swath of hail was observed by numerous storm chasers along Ranch Road 2999 east of Texas State Highway 70 northwest of Matador. Hail ranged in size from quarters to ping pong ball size.

Numerous storm chasers reported a swath of extremely large hail west of Matador along US Highway 62/70. Hail ranged in size from quarter size to three inches in diameter. No damage was included with the reports.

Numerous storm chasers reported a swath of extremely large hail along Farm to Market Road 684 west of Roaring Springs. Hail ranged in size from two inches in diameter to baseball size. No damage was included with the reports.
Several storm chasers and an NWS cooperative weather observer reported a swath of hail in the immediate vicinity of Roaring Springs. Hail ranged in size from quarters to golf ball size.
An NWS cooperative weather observer reported ping pong ball size hail on the northeast side of Matador.
